# czc-v2026.10.29.2 (0.2.19.3)

Gateway fixes for Codex clients and for Anthropic-backed Responses / Chat
Completions routes. Upstream "servers are overloaded" and "Codex is at
capacity" errors on the WebSocket path now retry or switch accounts instead
of failing the request with a 502. Anthropic content-policy refusals relayed
to OpenAI-format clients are now recorded as provider errors and are no longer
labelled as retryable server errors.

## Changes since czc-v2026.10.29.1

### Gateway: OpenAI WebSocket overload and rate-limit errors

Production logs for 2026-10-28 and 2026-10-29 showed about 1,250 upstream
WebSocket `error` events per day with `server_is_overloaded`
("Our servers are currently overloaded") and about 230 with
`turn_rate_limit_exceeded` ("Codex is at capacity") or
`usage_limit_reached`. Every one of them was returned to the client as a 502,
and the gateway never tried another account (the ops log's upstream attempts
list was empty).

The HTTP streaming path, the client WebSocket path and the WebSocket→HTTP
bridge already hand these errors to the account scheduler. The upstream
WebSocket v2 forwarder did not. Now:

- If the error arrives before anything has been sent to the client, the
  forwarder returns an account failover: 503 (request-scoped overload, with a
  short same-account retry first) or 429 (rate limit). The handler then waits
  and retries or switches accounts, as on the other paths.
- If output has already reached the client, behaviour is unchanged: the error
  is sent to the client with the overload code rewritten to the retryable
  `server_error`.
- Account state updates (temporary overload marks, rate-limit persistence)
  still run once, as before.
- The `error_event` log line now includes `wrote_downstream` and
  `client_output_started`, so it is visible whether an error came before or
  after the client started receiving output.

Known limit: most overload errors arrived right after the model started
reasoning. If that reasoning event had already been sent to the client, the
request cannot be switched and this release does not change the result for
it. The new log fields show how often that happens.

### Gateway: Anthropic upstream 4xx on Responses / Chat Completions routes

When an Anthropic upstream (for example the Devin2Claude bridge) rejected a
request with a 400 (content policy, cyber verification), requests on
`/v1/responses` and `/v1/chat/completions` were recorded in the ops error log
as a platform internal error with no upstream status (141 cases in 24 hours),
and the client got error code `server_error`, which Codex retries.

On the four routes that translate Anthropic responses into OpenAI format:

- The upstream status and an `http_error` attempt are recorded, so the ops
  log attributes the error to the provider.
- A 4xx is returned as `invalid_request_error`, and a 429 as
  `rate_limit_error`. 5xx and other failover statuses are unchanged.

## VERSION

`0.2.19.3`

## Upgrade guidance

- No database migration. No configuration change.
- Replace the binary and restart `sub2api.service`.

## Compatibility

- Overloaded / rate-limited Codex WebSocket requests may take a little longer
  (one same-account retry or an account switch) instead of failing.
- Clients of Anthropic-backed Responses / Chat Completions routes now receive
  `invalid_request_error` instead of `server_error` for upstream 4xx
  rejections. HTTP status codes are unchanged.

## Verification

Passed:

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go vet -tags unit ./internal/...`,
  `gofmt`.
- `go test -count=1 -tags unit ./...`: all 61 packages pass.
- `go test -count=1 ./...`: all packages pass.
- New tests: WebSocket v2 overload and rate-limit errors before client output
  return an account failover (503 request-scoped / 429) without writing to the
  client or falling back to same-account HTTP; Anthropic upstream 400 on
  Responses and Chat Completions routes records the upstream status and
  returns `invalid_request_error`. Both fail without the fix.
- Updated test: the WebSocket v2 usage-limit test now expects the 429 account
  failover instead of a locally written 429.
- Frontend `vue-tsc -b` and `vite build` for the embedded admin UI.

Failed or skipped:

- golangci-lint was not run (not installed on the build host).
- `-tags=integration` and `-tags=e2e` suites were not run; no repository or
  migration code changed.
- Frontend unit tests were not run; no frontend code changed.
- The failover was not tested against a live upstream overload before deploy;
  it is checked after deploy through the ops error log.

## Rollback

Redeploy `czc-v2026.10.29.1`, or restore the backup
`/opt/sub2api/sub2api.bak.czc-v2026.10.29.2-<UTC timestamp>` created during
this deploy and restart `sub2api.service`. There is no migration, so no
database rollback is needed.
